impact.affected_asset: Source-bridge custody and other users' liquidity for the same fee-on-transfer token.
impact.attacker_capability: A contract user can obtain a destination-chain claim/mint for nominal X after depositing a fee-on-transfer token that credits less than X to the source bridge, then bridge the full claimed amount back.
impact.security_effect: Cross-chain token backing deficit that can draw on other users' liquidity and eventually deny service for the affected token.

causal_trace.summary: A user supplies a fee-on-transfer token and requests bridging nominal amount X from Mainnet to Rollover R1.
The Mainnet bridge receives X minus token fees while a Merkle deposit receipt records the full nominal X.
The R1 claim creates a TokenPair and mints full X; after bridging that full amount back, a Mainnet claim attempts to transfer X although original custody was only X minus fees.
The reported full-X return transfer consumes liquidity belonging to other users of the same token and can eventually deny service to those users.

failure.operation: A source-chain return claim transfers nominal X despite source custody having received only X minus transfer fees.

primary_invariant.statement: The amount represented by a cross-chain deposit receipt and resulting claim must not exceed the amount of the bridged token actually received into source-chain custody.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The flow records the requested nominal amount X rather than the balance delta after a fee-on-transfer token transfer, allowing receipt and mint accounting to exceed custody.

quality.review_notes: The primary audit report explicitly describes the mechanism, sample balance-delta mitigation, and states PR 87 and PR 91 were solved and Spearbit verified. The bundle contains neither the reviewed source snapshot nor those PR diffs/tests, and contains no execution trace or test result; exact implementation, reentrancy protection, and reproducibility remain unverified independently.

remediation.invariant_restored: The bridge either records the actual balance increase as the bridged amount or rejects transfers where received amount differs from the requested nominal amount, preventing claims from exceeding custody.
mitigation_classes: reject nominal transfers whose received balance delta differs from requested amount
ERC-777 reentrancy protection when implementing the transfer flow
